Surreal still-life scene: a worn rustic wooden table stretching across the full width of the frame and bleeding off the bottom edge, in front of a pale hazy plaster wall, hard side light. In the CENTER of the table stands a small round clay flower pot tightly wrapped and cracked by thick old roots climbing over its rim, now EMPTY and abandoned, with dark soil spilled beside it. Immediately to the RIGHT of the pot, the young leafy tree sapling that just climbed out of it is WALKING away by itself toward the right side of the table, its exposed roots acting as little legs in mid-stride, leafy crown upright, a trail of crumbled soil connecting the pot to the plant. The sapling stands about two and a half times taller than the pot, the same scale as a sapling that lived in that pot. Pot and walking plant sit LOW, entirely inside the bottom half of the image. The vast ENTIRE UPPER HALF is bright, pale, hazy and empty, fading to near-white at the top.
